one_line: A shared mountain expedition UI for supervising long-running agent work.
what_it_does: Turns goals, blockers, approvals, evidence, and completion checks into a stateful expedition shared by a human and an AI agent.
leverage_rationale: The structured mission state, deterministic verification, blocker geography, and human-only route decisions make WebMCP central to the intended human-agent collaboration rather than a UI convenience.
leverage_evidence: Claims 18 native WebMCP tools with closed JSON schemas.
Tools operate on mission semantics through the same validated command engine as the UI.
Agent reports blockers and requests consequential human decisions in shared live state.
execution_rationale: The description presents a coherent, unusually complete workflow, but the packet has no video and image inspection was unavailable, so end-to-end completion is only claimed.
execution_evidence: Describes camps, blockers, route forks, evidence attachment, deterministic verification, and locked Summit completion.
Live demo is reported alive and four gallery images are reported.
impact_rationale: Long-running AI execution with approvals, blockers, and proof is a concrete problem for developers and technical leads; the proposed shared execution model addresses it directly.
impact_evidence: Explicit target audience is developers and technical leads supervising long-running AI execution.
Human authorization and evidence-before-completion directly address lost context and unsafe continuation.
creativity_rationale: The mountain-as-execution-state metaphor is memorable and deeply integrated with blockers, uncertainty, routes, and verification.
creativity_evidence: Mission state becomes mountain geography with camps, fog, crevasses, weather, and Summit gating.
Real blockers fracture the route and cosmetic progress is prevented.
usability_note: The metaphor and explicit decision gates appear understandable, though dense state may require onboarding.
red_flags: No submitted video or transcript; execution claims cannot be fully checked.
standouts: Strong shared-state metaphor and explicit human authorization boundary.
advance_reason: High-quality concept with strong WebMCP leverage and distinctive interaction model; execution should be validated in a later observed stage.

one_line: An evidence-backed incident review studio where agents investigate and humans authorize.
what_it_does: Lets an agent inspect bounded incident evidence, run deterministic counterfactual replays, draft a review gate, and hand the final decision to a human.
leverage_rationale: Structured evidence and staged tool availability create a reliable investigation workflow while preserving a hard human-only authorization boundary that generic UI driving would handle less safely.
leverage_evidence: Agent selects incidents and inspects synchronized bounded evidence through WebMCP.
Deterministic replay keeps a $142K trigger blocked while a benign control remains allowed.
Agent can verify but cannot create the human decision.
execution_rationale: The central incident-to-replay-to-human-gate workflow is coherent and specific, but no video evidence is supplied.
execution_evidence: Concrete synthetic procurement incident and spending-limit scenario.
Description specifies investigation, clean replay, draft gate, and visible human review transition.
Live demo reported alive.
impact_rationale: Autonomous-agent incidents and unsafe authorization are a clear operational problem, and the product directly supports accountable review.
impact_evidence: Specific failure mode: instruction-like supplier content led to attempted $142,000 purchase against a $50,000 limit.
Separates evidence-heavy investigation from consequential human authorization.
creativity_rationale: The investigation/authorization separation is a strong, safety-oriented interaction model with staged capabilities and counterfactual replay.
creativity_evidence: Core principle 'Agents investigate. Humans authorize.' is consistently embodied.
Capability changes throughout the investigation rather than exposing one unrestricted agent surface.
usability_note: A bounded evidence studio and visible gate should fit incident-review workflows; density may be substantial.
red_flags: No video or transcript; execution is claimed rather than observed.
standouts: Clear safety boundary and deterministic counterfactual demonstration.
advance_reason: Specific high-impact workflow with unusually strong WebMCP leverage and credible safety design.

one_line: A WebMCP production-scheduling sandbox with isolated drafts and human approval.
what_it_does: Lets people or agents inspect a synthetic paint-line factory, optimize and compare draft schedules, then request human review without agent commit authority.
leverage_rationale: Stable structured scheduling operations, protected constraints, deterministic optimization, and human-only commit materially improve reliability over DOM automation in a stateful operational workflow.
leverage_evidence: Tools inspect machines, orders, calendars, constraints, move stable-ID orders, optimize, compare, and request review.
Protected orders and overtime validity are enforced in the product.
Agent may request review but cannot commit.
execution_rationale: The draft/baseline comparison and approval flow is well specified, though evidence is packaging plus claims because no video is supplied.
execution_evidence: Concrete candidate metrics: six fewer paint changes, one fewer late order, one more on-time order.
Live factory visualization and alive demo are reported.
impact_rationale: Production scheduling has a real operational audience and the sandbox provides credible value through safer alternative exploration and review.
impact_evidence: Targets production scheduling and synthetic automotive paint-line constraints.
Compares makespan, overtime, paint changes, and late/on-time orders.
creativity_rationale: The human-agent scheduling boundary is a fresh and ambitious treatment of a known operations problem.
creativity_evidence: Isolated scenario plus committed baseline and human-only approval are integrated into the interaction model.
usability_note: Structured comparisons and approval reduce risk, though factory scheduling is inherently dense.
red_flags: No video/transcript; central workflow not visually verified.
standouts: Strong constraint and approval semantics rather than simple schedule editing.
advance_reason: High practical value and major WebMCP delta; merits advancement pending observed execution.

one_line: An agent-operated ASWB exam diagnostic and adaptive study coach.
what_it_does: Runs a diagnostic through WebMCP, measures readiness, persists results, and builds a dated study prescription visible on the page.
leverage_rationale: The agent can operate a shared diagnostic and persistent readiness state while the human answers questions, making structured state and repeatability meaningfully better than ordinary UI driving.
leverage_evidence: 11 WebMCP tools move the shared readiness UI and study plan.
Readiness persists in localStorage between visits.
Agent carries exam-date context and retrieves structured readiness history.
execution_rationale: The workflow and dual API compatibility are detailed, but there are no gallery images, video frames, or transcript, and the demo uses only six sample questions.
execution_evidence: Describes diagnostic, readiness ring, weak-area ranking, and dated week-by-week prescription.
Explicitly says production question bank is private and demo uses six original samples.
impact_rationale: ASWB candidates and exam-prep providers have a concrete measurement-and-prescription need addressed by the product.
impact_evidence: Identifies ASWB exam preparation as the primary audience.
Diagnostic-to-readiness-to-plan loop directly matches the stated need.
creativity_rationale: Agent-operated persistent assessment is a useful synthesis but remains within a familiar adaptive study-coach category.
creativity_evidence: Shared human answering and agent measurement loop with returning-agent continuity.
usability_note: Visible progress and study prescription are approachable; limited demo content constrains confidence.
red_flags: Underlying exam-prep product appears pre-existing; WebMCP addition is the judged submission.
standouts: Persistent readiness state and compatibility with both WebMCP API spellings.
advance_reason: Credible education use case and meaningful shared-state leverage, despite thin execution evidence.

one_line: An agent-native gym operations ERP centered on a tactical visual floor plan.
what_it_does: Combines facility floor operations, maintenance, class scheduling, churn risk, retention campaigns, and telemetry in a reactive workspace.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP can update equipment state and schedules in shared live views, but much of the broad ERP functionality could likely be driven through a general agent with friction.
leverage_evidence: Claims live WebMCP tool execution updates maintenance state and moves classes.
Trainer conflict and capacity validation are visible workflow constraints.
Agent HUD and real-time floor state unify operations.
execution_rationale: The surface area is ambitious and internally coherent, but breadth creates uncertainty and no video transcript is supplied.
execution_evidence: Claims 2D blueprint across five zones, scheduling modal, churn radar, campaign dispatch, and telemetry sandbox.
Seven gallery images and alive demo reported.
impact_rationale: Gym managers and coaches have concrete coordination and retention problems, and the consolidated operational view plausibly addresses them.
impact_evidence: Specific facility-management problems: maintenance, trainer conflicts, capacity, and member churn.
Provides targeted retention vouchers and operational telemetry.
creativity_rationale: A tactical floor commander metaphor applied to gym ERP is distinctive and ambitious, with several connected operational loops.
creativity_evidence: Tony Stark-style visual command center and reactive blueprint are pursued across maintenance and scheduling.
usability_note: Single workspace is valuable, but high-density ERP breadth may overwhelm operators.
red_flags: Very broad scope; no video/transcript to establish which flows actually work.
standouts: Visual floor plan as an operational control surface rather than another form-heavy ERP.
advance_reason: Ambitious and high-value operational concept with adequate claimed evidence, pending observed validation.

one_line: A merchant-governed storefront that reshapes itself around a shopper’s expressed context.
what_it_does: Uses an AI companion and structured commerce tools to select merchant-authored scenarios, content blocks, proof, imagery, and purchase controls for relevance-first shopping.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP changes the storefront from a fixed page into a shared, structured decision surface where the companion composes controlled views rather than merely clicking UI elements.
leverage_evidence: Companion shares a need, selects and composes the on-page experience.
Reusable layouts expose controlled fields for copy, imagery, proof, and purchase controls.
Structured commerce tools operate on merchant-governed scenarios.
execution_rationale: Multiple concrete shopper scenarios and content systems indicate intentional scope, but there is no video and no gallery frame verification available.
execution_evidence: Describes city-use, cabin/airline-fit, analytical specification, and gift scenarios.
Nine gallery images and alive demo reported.
impact_rationale: Shoppers benefit from reduced information overload and context-specific evidence, while merchants retain control over claims and layout.
impact_evidence: Scenarios map product facts to travel, work, photography, and gifting needs.
Relevance-first persuasion foregrounds fewer stronger reasons at decision time.
creativity_rationale: Dynamic merchant-authored storefront composition is a memorable interaction model that goes beyond recommendation into contextual presentation.
creativity_evidence: One bag store becomes multiple focused storefronts without unbounded agent-generated claims.
Combines layouts, evidence blocks, and assets under governance.
usability_note: Focused views can reduce shopping cognitive load; scenario switching and trust need careful UX.
red_flags: No video/transcript; composition behavior is claimed rather than observed.
standouts: Strong merchant-control answer to agent personalization and hallucinated merchandising.
advance_reason: Highly differentiated commerce concept with transformative claimed WebMCP leverage.

one_line: A shared pixel canvas where humans choose zones and agents paint attributed sprites.
what_it_does: Lets humans and browser agents collaboratively stamp validated ASCII-grid art onto a live shared 256x256 canvas with attribution and realtime updates.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP enables any browser agent to participate in the live shared canvas without MCP App compatibility or installation, with structured validation and shared state.
leverage_evidence: Three tools divide display name, zone selection, and validated stamping.
Canvas updates are shared through Supabase Realtime and attributed.
WebMCP removes the prior requirement for an MCP-compatible app.
execution_rationale: The project describes a focused end-to-end loop with validation and attribution, but no video transcript is supplied.
execution_evidence: Tool registration depends on display name and validates palette, bounds, zone, and budget.
Reports shared pixels visible across browser, ChatGPT, and Claude; live demo reported alive.
impact_rationale: Collaborative creative play and community expression are legitimate, and the shared-canvas format gives agents an accessible participatory role.
impact_evidence: Explicit r/place-inspired shared canvas and human-agent co-creation.
Attribution and realtime multi-surface visibility support community participation.
creativity_rationale: The deliberate division of human spatial intent and agent pixel execution is simple, memorable, and well matched to the medium.
creativity_evidence: Humans pick the spot while agents place pixels.
ASCII sprite plus palette legend is a constrained agent-to-visual interaction.
usability_note: Narrow tool roles and visible canvas feedback should make participation easy.
red_flags: Origin appears pre-existing as a ChatGPT/Claude app; WebMCP extension is the submission delta.
standouts: Clear agent/human role split and cross-surface shared canvas.
advance_reason: Excellent focused demonstration of WebMCP enabling agent participation in a shared creative state.

one_line: A conversational future-home floor-plan simulator for inventing and editing living spaces.
what_it_does: Maintains structured rooms, walls, openings, furniture, and equipment while WebMCP agents inspect, propose, validate, and apply natural-language design changes.
leverage_rationale: Structured floor-plan state and validate-before-apply operations make natural-language collaborative editing safer and more repeatable than generic coordinate-based UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Agent can inspect, propose, validate, and apply floor-plan changes.
Underlying data is structured and visual output is generated from it.
Exports current plan as PNG or PDF.
execution_rationale: The stated workflow is coherent and a 212-second video exists, but transcript is absent and visual review could not be completed.
execution_evidence: Demo video reported at 212 seconds with title identifying WebMCP.
Concrete supported edits include resize, split, and parking-space conversion.
Four gallery images reported.
impact_rationale: Accessible conversational floor planning serves aspiring designers and people imagining unconventional future living arrangements, though practical audience fit is less established.
impact_evidence: Natural-language design lowers specialized-control burden.
Explicitly supports imagined devices and living systems beyond conventional furniture.
creativity_rationale: The combination of conversational architectural editing and invention of future living systems is original and ambitious.
creativity_evidence: Future floor-plan simulator frames home design as a medium for inventing nonexistent ways of living.
WebMCP workflow separates proposal, validation, and application.
usability_note: Natural-language edits and exact export are approachable, with validation helping prevent destructive changes.
red_flags: Video exists but transcript and inspectable frames were unavailable in this review run.
standouts: Strong imaginative scope grounded in structured floor-plan semantics.
advance_reason: Distinctive creative tool with strong structured-edit leverage and a claimed long demo video.

one_line: A persistent shopping decision workspace shared by a human and an AI agent.
what_it_does: Tracks goals, budgets, priorities, shortlist, rejected products, comparisons, insights, and decision history while an agent challenges and updates the live decision.
leverage_rationale: The agent accesses and updates structured decision context that shoppers otherwise must restate manually, creating meaningful shared-state value though the underlying actions remain conventional shopping operations.
leverage_evidence: Agent inspects current decision, goal, shortlist, comparisons, and rejected products.
Agent can challenge choices, find alternatives, surface them, and update the decision.
Decision engine evaluates products against actual requirements.
execution_rationale: The state model and intended flow are coherent, but no gallery or video evidence is submitted, limiting claimed execution confidence.
execution_evidence: Explicit structured decision state includes history and insights.
Live demo reported alive; packaging screenshot only.
impact_rationale: Persistent decision context addresses a real shopping friction: separating conversational recommendations from the user’s evolving shortlist and preferences.
impact_evidence: Targets users who compare, reject, and prioritize products over time.
Human retains decision authority while agent participates.
creativity_rationale: The decision-first framing and agent challenge loop are a fresh synthesis within shopping assistants.
creativity_evidence: Agent participates in an existing decision rather than starting a disconnected recommendation conversation.
Decision history and rejected options are first-class state.
usability_note: Persistent context can simplify comparison, but the breadth of decision state may require clear summarization.
red_flags: No video or gallery evidence, so execution is thinly supported.
standouts: Explicitly preserves rejected options and decision history for agent reasoning.
advance_reason: Solid shared-decision concept with meaningful leverage; execution evidence is the main uncertainty.

one_line: A conversational assistant that populates a visible Indonesian individual tax-return draft.
what_it_does: Translates plain-language salary, deductions, and family information into section-level tax-form fields while users review the visible draft before submission.
leverage_rationale: Structured section-level tools can translate conversational facts into rigid tax classifications while preserving a reviewable shared draft, materially reducing navigation and field-mapping errors.
leverage_evidence: WebMCP exposes section-level tools directly to the assistant.
Workflow conducts a plain-language interview and populates a visible draft.
User remains in control of review and submission.
execution_rationale: The problem and workflow are concrete, and frame sheets are claimed, but no video transcript and no visual inspection were available; end-to-end operation is not confirmed.
execution_evidence: Addresses Indonesia Coretax individual return (1770 S) complexity.
Claims conversational extraction, visible form population, and human review boundary.
Live demo reported alive.
impact_rationale: Millions of individual filers facing confusing classifications and error-prone government forms are a specific, substantial audience with a direct usability problem.
impact_evidence: Identifies salaried workers and cross-generational users struggling to map life events to tax classifications.
Cites large filing/account figures in the submission text, while solution directly targets procedural confusion.
creativity_rationale: Conversational extraction into a reviewable government tax draft is a strong practical application, though the interaction model is a familiar assistant pattern.
creativity_evidence: Keeps complex detailed form visible while exposing semantic section tools rather than hiding form logic.
Human review-before-submission is integrated into the concept.
usability_note: Plain-language intake can reduce classification burden; tax accuracy and review clarity are critical.
red_flags: Tax-domain correctness is high stakes and not independently demonstrated in the packet.
No transcript; visual evidence not confirmed.
standouts: Excellent audience/problem specificity and visible human review boundary.
advance_reason: High-impact, concrete WebMCP use case with credible safety framing; observed execution and tax correctness require follow-up.
